general: Extract every entity of the supplied types. Return exact spans from the query. Leave other text unlabelled.

classes.name: Task
classes.description: Refers to a particular research task or problem within a specific AI research field.
rules: TA1 Annotate the name of the specific task, such as machine translation or object detection.
TA2 Examples: "speech synthesis", "information retrieval", "Feature extraction", "dimension reduction", "speech recognition".

classes.name: Location
classes.description: Refers to a specific geographical or structural location.
rules: LO1 This includes but is not limited to: places (e.g., parks, landmarks), bridges, cities, towns, villages, areas and other distinct regions.
LO2 Examples: "Chișinău", "Paris", "Montreal", "Scotiabank Theatre Toronto", "TIFF Bell Lightbox".

classes.name: Organization
classes.description: Refers to a structured group, institution, company, or association.
rules: OR1 This category covers a diverse range of organizations, including businesses, non-profits, educational institutions, and government agencies.
OR2 Examples: "Unimation", "IAPR", "Audio Engineering Society", "National Science Foundation", "National Aeronautics and Space Administration".

classes.name: Metric
classes.description: Refers to evaluation metrics used to assess the performance of AI models and algorithms.
rules: ME1 Annotate specific metrics like F1-score.
ME2 Examples: "mean squared error", "DCG", "maximum likelihood", "Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation", "MSE".

classes.name: ProgrammingLanguage
classes.description: Refers to a programming language used in the development of AI applications and research.
rules: PL1 Annotate the name of the programming language, such as Java and Python.
PL2 Examples: "Java", "R", "CLIPS", "Python", "C + +".

classes.name: Product
classes.description: Refers to a product, system, or toolkit related to Artificial Intelligence.
rules: PR1 This includes specific AI-enabled products (e.g., robots like Pepper), systems (e.g., facial recognition systems), and toolkits (e.g., Tensorflow and PyTorch).
PR2 Examples: "MATLAB", "Programmable Universal Machine for Assembly", "industrial robot", "opinion-based recommender system", "Octave".

classes.name: Algorithm
classes.description: Refers to an algorithmic procedure or computational model used in Artificial Intelligence research.
rules: AL1 This category includes algorithms (e.g., decision trees) and models (e.g., CNN and LSTM).
AL2 Examples: "principal component analysis", "linear discriminant analysis", "gradient descent", "Support vector machine", "recurrent neural network".

classes.name: Country
rules: CO1 Examples: "Netherlands", "Japan", "Germany", "Canada", "Australia".

classes.name: Person
classes.description: Refers to an individual's name that is not a researcher.
rules: PE1 Examples: "Francis Ford Coppola", "Michael Jackson", "John Wayne", "Rita Hayworth", "Dean Martin".

classes.name: Researcher
classes.description: Refers to an individual engaged in research activities within the field of Artificial Intelligence (AI), including professors, Ph.D. students, and researchers in academia, research institutions, and companies.
rules: RE1 If a person is involved in AI research, label them as a researcher entity instead of a person entity.
RE2 Examples: "Jürgen Schmidhuber", "Seymour Papert", "Victor Scheinman", "Scheinman", "X.Y. Feng".

classes.name: Field
classes.description: Refers to a specific research area or subfield within Artificial Intelligence.
rules: FI1 Also annotate acronyms such as NLP.
FI2 Examples: "deep learning", "pattern recognition", "image processing", "reinforcement learning", "natural language processing".

classes.name: Conference
classes.description: Refers to a research conference or journal in the field of Artificial Intelligence.
rules: CON1 This category includes conferences where AI research is presented and published.
CON2 Examples: "AAAI", "1982 Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence", "SIGGRAPH", "Symposium on Geometry Processing", "International Journal of Computer Vision".

classes.name: University
classes.description: Refers to an educational institution of higher learning.
rules: UN1 Label organizations that are universities as 'university'' entities.
UN2 Examples: "University of Toronto", "Cambridge", "University of Groningen", "MIT", "Brown University".

classes.name: Other
classes.description: Refers to named entities that are not included in any other category.
rules: OT1 Examples: "unsupervised methods", "topological properties", "audio signal", "eigenfaces", "intelligent agents".
